prompt: One of the ways that advertising benefits society is by encouraging the development of better
explanation: Products. Advertising benefits society in a variety of ways. One way is by encouraging the development of new and better products. When one business successfully advertises and sells a product, its competitors often try to develop a better product in order to attract customers. This type of advertising competition also benefits society by providing a wide range of products at reasonable prices. Developing better commercials, packaging, and campaigns benefit businesses rather than society.

prompt: What do many advertising agencies do with the money they have accumulated as a result of periods of positive cash flow?
explanation: Reinvest the funds. Smart advertising agencies reinvest some of the money left over during periods of large positive cash flow back into the business. Many agencies take advantage of positive cash flow to make improvements in the company or to put aside some funds to cover expenses during slow times. Agencies would not use excess funds to buy personal items. Smart agencies do not spend all available cash, but save some for emergencies. Purchasing excess supplies is not a good use of extra funds because the agency will have storage costs.

prompt: The bottom line on a graphic design business's profit-and-loss statement indicates
explanation: Net income. The net income, or bottom line, is a graphic design business's final profit. It is the money remaining after operating expenses are subtracted from gross profit. Net income is the amount of money a business is able to keep after paying all expenses. Total costs are all of a business's expenses. Gross revenue is all the money earned by a business before expenses are subtracted. Net worth is the total value of the business.

prompt: Who is responsible for developing a quality culture in a public relations business?
explanation: All employees. A quality culture cannot exist in a public relations business unless all employees are involved. Although some employees are more directly involved, everyone must participate. For example, management must provide the guidance and direction as well as the tools necessary for employees to do quality work. The production staff must do their best to produce a quality product, and salespeople must provide quality service to customers. Support personnel, such as accounting clerks and delivery people, also must be committed to doing a quality job. Everyone must do their part and work together to develop a quality culture.

prompt: One reason companies may not be placing as many advertisements in newspapers and magazines as they did twenty years ago is because
choices: consumers are not buying as many goods and services.
print advertising is becoming more and more expensive.
more consumers are getting information from the Internet.
advertising messages contain too much technical information.
explanation: More consumers are getting information from the Internet. With the development of PCs and Internet capa-bilities, the means of communicating information quickly has increased dramatically. Many publishers are putting full or partial forms of their magazines and newspapers on their web sites. Contemporary consumers are pressed for time and disposable income to purchase the print collateral. Therefore, more and more consumers are turning on computers and getting the information they need, when they want it; and many are not buying as many newspapers or magazines as in the past. Consumers are buying more than they did twenty years ago. Print advertising is not becoming more expensive. Advertising messages usually do not contain a lot of technical information.

prompt: When posting information on a web page, the hypertags you will use to mark paragraphs in your document are
explanation:
and

. The hypertag

tells the browser to begin a new paragraph and

tells it to end that paragraph. Notice there is a difference; the end symbol includes a slash mark. Both markings are necessary if the browser is to work correctly on the page. Using

twice simply repeats the new paragraph hypertag. The symbols and , and and are not hypertags.

prompt: An example of how modern technology is impacting and changing the advertising industry is the placement of
explanation: Banner ads on the Internet. The technology of computers and global communication is opening up a new avenue to advertisers that want to reach a worldwide market. The development of the Internet has created a new advertising medium. Now, many agencies are expanding their services to include developing and plac-ing banner ads and other types of advertising spots on the Internet. The involvement of advertising on the Internet will continue to grow as this new medium evolves. Billboards, television commercials, and public-service announcements are types of advertising that have been in existence for a long time.

prompt: Which of the following is a reason why media production companies should evaluate speculative risks:
choices: To determine the potential for loss
To reduce the possibility of theft
To estimate the level of property damage
explanation: To determine the potential for loss. Speculative risks are chances of loss that may result in loss, no change, or gain. When a media production company takes a speculative risk, there is always the possibility of failure. Therefore, before taking speculative risks, companies usually evaluate them in order to determine the potential for loss. Companies may decide not to take the risk because the potential for loss is too high. Companies cannot obtain insurance for speculative risks. Companies usually purchase insurance to cover losses due to theft or property damage.

prompt: In which of the following situations might a small creative boutique be able to reduce the premiums it pays for insurance coverage:
explanation: Buys from its professional organization. Insurance is a major expense for most small creative boutiques because small businesses often cannot obtain the same low rates that are available to large corporations. One way for small businesses to reduce their premiums is to buy insurance coverage through a professional organization. Many professional organizations that represent businesses in specific industries are able to offer lower cost coverage to their members, because together they constitute a large group. Acquiring addi-tional protection and decreasing the amount of the deductible usually increases the premium. Businesses that are self-insured do not pay for coverage but handle their own losses.

prompt: When preparing a profit-and-loss statement, what does the photography studio subtract from gross profit to determine net profit or loss?
explanation: Operating expenses. The final line on a profit-and-loss statement indicates the photography studio's net profit or loss. Net profit is the money remaining after operating expenses are subtracted from gross profit. If the studio has a net loss, there is no money remaining and the business is in debt. The formula for calculat-ing net profit or loss is gross sales minus net sales, minus cost of goods sold, minus operating expenses. Studios subtract cost of goods sold from net sales to calculate gross profit. Sales returns are subtracted from gross sales to determine net sales. Total purchases are part of the cost of goods sold category.

prompt: What are advertising agencies required to follow in order to provide secure and safe workplaces for their employees?
explanation: OSHA standards. The Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) is responsible for establishing and enforcing safety and health standards in the workplace. The purpose of OSHA is to make sure that all employees have a secure and safe environment in which to work. Advertising agencies are required to follow OSHA standards and maintain their workplaces accordingly. The Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) are not responsible for workplace security.

prompt: Which of the following is a true statement about safety hazards in the workplace:
choices: Safety hazards are obvious to most people.
Poor housekeeping can cause safety hazards.
Safety hazards are the same for most businesses.
Equipment that needs repair is not a safety hazard.
explanation: Poor housekeeping can cause safety hazards. Cluttered areas of the workplace can create safety hazards. For example, people can trip over items lying on the floor, slip on liquids that have been spilled, or be injured when poorly stacked containers fall over. Safety hazards differ according to the kind of business. Equip-ment that needs repair may have loose parts or malfunction in a way that would injure workers. Safety hazards are not obvious to most people unless they have been taught to recognize them.

prompt: Why do advertising agencies with excessive debts often file Chapter 7 bankruptcy?
explanation: To liquidate. Federal law provides protection for businesses when they are unable to pay their debts by allowing them to file for bankruptcy. Chapter 7 bankruptcy involves liquidating the business and selling the assets in order to pay creditors a portion of what the business owes them. The end result of Chapter 7 bank-ruptcy is that the business is released from debts, but all the assets have been liquidated and the business no longer exists. Chapter 11 bankruptcy allows a business to reorganize, which may involve obtaining addi-tional financing. Chapter 7 bankruptcy does not allow a business to consolidate.

prompt: What do federal regulations concerning workplace issues require direct-mail businesses to provide to qualified individuals with disabilities?
explanation: Reasonable accommodations. Reasonable accommodations involve providing some type of assistance to qualified employees who have limitations in order for them to do their jobs. Federal regulations require businesses to provide reasonable accommodations so that qualified employees with disabilities have the opportunity to obtain or keep their jobs. Providing reasonable accommodations does not mean changing the way that a company does business, but it does involve making reasonable concessions such as a simple modification of equipment. Federal regulations do not require businesses to provide preferential treatment or psychological counseling to qualified individuals with disabilities. Businesses provide compensation packages to all employees based on the type of work they do, their qualifications, their education, their seniority, etc.

prompt: When preparing a complex written report, what is the advantage of developing a detailed sentence outline?
explanation: Summarizes material to include. An advantage of developing a detailed sentence outline is that it forces writers to summarize the information that they will include in the complex report. Once the material is sum-marized and organized in sentence format, the basis for the report is complete. Writing the actual report from this type of outline is fairly easy because of the detailed summary. A disadvantage is that this type of outline requires a lot of preparation. The outline does not interpret technical information or develop a logical conclusion. That is the responsibility of the writer.

prompt: Which of the following would be most useful in conducting a staff meeting:
explanation: A planned agenda. Managers who conduct staff meetings are more likely to have a smooth-running meeting when they take time to prepare an agenda of the subjects that need to be covered in the meeting. An agenda also helps to ensure that no important topics are forgotten. It may be useful to have a specific time to start and to stop the meeting or a list of the staff who will be at the meeting, but those factors will not help conduct the meeting. A formal manner is not always appropriate and may create the wrong atmosphere.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of an ethical situation in which an employee is involved in communicating information:
choices: Spreading rumors that were overheard in the lounge
Asking a loyal client to write a complimentary letter
Telling a coworker that some employees will be laid off
Making negative statements about the quality of a product
explanation: Asking a loyal customer to write a complimentary letter. It is ethical for an employee to ask loyal clients who are satisfied with the advertising service they receive to write complimentary letters to management. Perhaps the employee is in line for a promotion and favorable comments from clients would be helpful. The employee is simply asking clients to pass on accurate and truthful information. The decision to write the letter is up to the client. It is unethical to tell a coworker that some employees will be laid off or to spread rumors that were overheard in the lounge. Employees should not make negative statements about the quality of a product. If they have concerns about quality, they should discuss the matter with management.

prompt: Which of the following is a marketing function that can be performed by channel intermediaries:
explanation: Promoting products. Channel intermediaries are persons or businesses that perform channel functions in an indirect channel of distribution. They can be responsible for such marketing functions as buying, selling, pricing, marking, storing, packaging, promoting, and financing. Recruiting workers for the business, training employees, and monitoring union activities are human resource activities, not marketing functions.

prompt: Customer satisfaction, employee contentment, and profit can be directly linked to
explanation: Ethical business practices. Studies have shown a strong relationship between customer satisfaction and a company's ethical behavior. Building customer loyalty gives a business a competitive advantage and is profitable. Taking care of employees tends to encourage employees to take care of business. Paying higher wages is not the only requirement for employee commitment. Pricing strategies can ensure profit but have little impact on employee commitment and customer loyalty. Customer satisfaction, employee contentment, and profit are not directly linked to automated distribution centers.

prompt: When preparing invoices, it is important to accurately state the terms of sale because they are
choices: wholesale costs for the items being sold.
discounts that affect the total amount due.
explanation: Discounts that affect the total amount due. Terms of sale are indicated as discounts on an invoice. There are several types of terms, such as ordinary and extra, that indicate the amount of discount that can be taken based on when the invoice is paid. For example, 3/10, N30 is an ordinary term that means that the purchaser may take a 3% discount if the invoice is paid within 10 days. After that time, the full amount is due. It is important to accurately state the terms of sale because errors may be costly to the seller. For example, if the terms read 30/10 instead of 3/10, the buyer would be entitled to a 30% discount for paying within 10 days. There is a significant difference between a 3% discount and a 30% discount. An extension is the unit price multiplied by the number of items purchased. Terms of sale are not the wholesale costs for the items being sold or restrictions on return policies.

prompt: Why is security an important consideration in setting up a specialty advertising business's storage area?
choices: To prevent the theft of goods
To prevent crowding the sales floor
explanation: To prevent the theft of goods. Goods in a specialty advertising business's storage area should be protected from employee pilferage and customer theft. Many businesses have specific policies regarding the security of the storage area such as allowing only authorized personnel to have access to the area. Keeping the storage area secure does not help employees to find stored items, improve the flow of merchandise to the sales floor, or prevent crowded conditions on the sales floor.

prompt: Businesses usually coordinate the distribution of their goods and services with the marketing activity of
explanation: Promotion. Businesses usually coordinate the distribution of their goods and services with the marketing activity of promotion in order to make sure that the goods and services are available when they are adver-tised. Businesses do not want to advertise special discounts or limited-time offers until those items are actually available. For example, advertising too early will upset customers because they cannot obtain the goods and services then. Management is not a marketing activity. Directing is a management activity that involves providing guidance to workers and work projects. Purchasing is a business activity that involves obtaining goods and services for use in the business or for resale.

prompt: What can producers do to overcome a problem with limited human resources?
explanation: Offer training and retraining. Human resources are the people who work to produce goods and services. Training and retraining helps workers to develop new skills and to do a better job. When resources are limited, producers are more likely to increase the use of automation and increase benefits. An increase in the use of natural resources, items that are found in nature, would not influence the supply of human resources.

prompt: Which of the following is important information that advertising specialty businesses consider when deciding whether it would be profitable to increase production:
explanation: Marginal cost. Marginal cost is the change in cost involved in increasing or decreasing production. It is often used to calculate the extra cost of producing one more item. For example, if an advertising specialty busi-ness produces 1,000 key chains each day and is considering increasing production to 1,100 per day, the business needs to know how much it will cost to produce 100 more key chains. If the marginal cost is low, the business might decide to increase production because it will also increase profitability. However, if pro-ducing 100 more key chains is expensive, it might not be profitable for the business to increase production. Cash flow is the movement of money, or cash, into and out of a business. Discretionary income is the amount of income people have left to spend or dispose of after they have paid their taxes. Finance charge is interest charged on the outstanding balance of a credit account.

prompt: If the Consumer Price Index was 126.4 in 2001 and 132.1 in 2002, what is the rate of inflation?
explanation: 4.5%. The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures the changes in price of specific goods and services used by the average household. The increase in price from month to month or from year to year indicates the level of inflation, which is the rise in prices. Inflation may be an economic problem if it increases rapidly. In order to calculate the rate of inflation based on CPI, subtract the CPI for 2001 from the CPI for 2002 (132.1 – 126.4 = 5.7). Divide the CPI increase by the 2001 CPI figure (5.7 ÷ 126.4 = .045). Then, multiply that figure by 100 to calculate the rate of inflation from 2001 to 2001 (.045 x 100 = 4.5%).

prompt: One reason why many underdeveloped countries are unable to trade successfully with other nations is that they lack
explanation: Investment money. Many underdeveloped countries do not have sufficient funds to invest in improving the economy because the people are poor and spend all they earn in order to survive. The people do not have disposable income to invest in companies, pay taxes to the government, or put in savings accounts. There-fore, the countries do not have access to additional funds that could be used to improve production and develop products to trade with other nations. Many underdeveloped countries have large national debts because they have borrowed money from prosperous nations. Most underdeveloped countries have the economic information they need but not the money necessary to implement economic programs. Strong government control is a characteristic of most underdeveloped countries.

prompt: The technology of electronic funds transfer (EFT) makes it possible for advertising agencies to move money
explanation: From one account to another. Electronic funds transfer (EFT) makes it possible to move money from one account to another by computer. Many advertising agencies use EFT to move money from their accounts to the accounts of their suppliers in order to pay bills. Agencies also use EFT to deposit employees' salaries directly into their checking accounts. The advantage of EFT is that it is fast and efficient and makes the funds available immediately upon deposit. The use of EFT does not mean that agencies do not need to pay income tax. Banks place actual currency in automated teller machines. The telegraphic process involves paying a sum of money at one location and wiring instructions to another location to pay that amount to someone.

prompt: In which of the following situations is it important for a new quick-print shop that intends to accept credit cards to shop around in order to obtain the best rate before selecting a credit-card company:
choices: Most sales will be mail order.
Average size of each sale will be large.
Sales will be made from a home.
Projected sales volume will be low.
explanation: Projected sales volume will be low. Quick-print shops that intend to accept credit cards should shop around before selecting a credit-card company in order to obtain the best rate. On average, banks and credit-card companies charge between 2.5% and 5.5% of a business's credit sales. Different banks and credit-card companies charge different rates depending on a business's sales volume and size of sales. As a rule, banks charge a business a higher rate if its total sales volume is low than they charge a business whose total sales volume is high. A business can save money by shopping around for a bank or credit-card company that offers a low rate, even if its sales volume is low. Banks and credit-card companies base their rates on sales volume and size of sales rather than on whether the sales are mail order or made from a home. Busi-nesses whose average size of each sale is large usually are charged low rates.

prompt: Besides financial statements, the most important document that an entrepreneur needs to get a loan from a bank is the
explanation: Business plan. A good business plan demonstrates to a prospective lender that an entrepreneur has the knowledge, managerial competence, and technical capability to run a successful business. It explains in detail how the business will operate. The marketing plan, product description, and company personnel are all part of a good business plan.

prompt: Information about marketing trends, competitors' activities, and new technology are examples of __________ marketing information.
explanation: External. External data provide information about the activities outside the advertising business. Sources of external information include libraries, federal and state planning agencies, trade journals, and marketing-research companies. Internal data are collected from sources within the business. Insufficient information is given to determine whether the data are primary or secondary.

prompt: Finding out how many people in a community spend money on a given product is an example of
explanation: Qualitative research. The aim of qualitative research is to explore and understand the attitudes, opinions, feelings, and behaviors of individuals or a group of individuals. In quantitative research, your aim is to deter-mine the relationship between one thing (an independent variable) and another (a dependent or outcome variable) in a population. Interviewing is a method of qualitative research, while gathering demographic information is a form of quantitative research.

prompt: What type of records will a graphic design business use to find out what it has ordered from a particular vendor?
explanation: Purchase. Purchase records include purchase orders and invoices that provide information about what goods were ordered, the quantity ordered, and from which vendor. Sales records provide data concerning cash and credit sales transactions. Promotional records provide information on a business's promotional efforts and the results of the promotions. Financial records provide data such as accounts payable, accounts receivable, fixed assets, and revenue information.

prompt: What internal records do many specialty advertising businesses monitor in order to obtain useful marketing information?
explanation: Sales reports. Specialty advertising businesses maintain and monitor sales records that contain information related to the goods that a business stocks and sells. This type of data helps a business to analyze what types of products are selling quickly and should be reordered to meet the wants and needs of its target market. Businesses also use the information in sales reports to identify slow-moving goods and make decisions about lowering prices or conducting special sales. Trade journals and industry projections are external sources of marketing information. Businesses often use marketing information to develop print advertisements that will appeal to their customers.

prompt: Information that a printing salesperson might record in a customer account profile includes the customer's
choices: sales volume and the names of key decision makers.
credit rating and overall corporate compensation plan.
quarterly profit margins and estimated sales potential.
product line expansion plans and employee turnover rates. Response Value Frequency Very likely 1 20 Likely 2 55 Somewhat likely 3 92 Unlikely 4 75 Very unlikely 5 33
explanation: Sales volume and the names of key decision makers. Creating an account profile helps printing salespeople keep track of prospects and customers. Profiles can aid sales managers in evaluating sales territories, salesperson workload, and establishing sales goals for their staff members. Account profiles often sum-marize general and detailed information about each customer. Information such as business name, address, telephone number, key contacts and decision makers, sales volume, sales potential, expansion plans, credit information, other suppliers, purchasing habits, and previous problems are often recorded in the customer profile. Information such as employee turnover rates and compensation plans are not usually data that are needed in the customer's profile. Although financial data such as quarterly profit statements might help salespeople plan their selling strategies, they are not always available for review.

prompt: In the following chart, which value represents the mode:
explanation: 3. Mode is the most common value in a set of responses to a question. It represents the answer that is most often given. In this example, 3 is the value given to the answer "Somewhat likely," and that is the answer given by the most respondents, 92. Marketers use the mode to measure tendencies of response and group data into smaller categories such as which response is the most common.

prompt: What part of a marketing-research report would be mentioned only briefly in an oral presentation?
explanation: Research methods. An oral presentation includes the same information as the written report although the oral presentation of this information is handled differently because there are limitations on the amount of time available to give an oral presentation. Consequently, oral reports focus on explaining the research findings, which include relevant information and pertinent data. Explaining the research methods used to collect the information is not as important as explaining other parts of the report. Therefore, the research methods would be mentioned only briefly, if at all, in an oral presentation. In some situations, take-home copies of handouts that explain the research methods and other parts of the written report might be available after the oral presentation.

prompt: When developing a targeted marketing strategy, why must advertisers first segment their potential audiences?
choices: Consumers like being described in different categories.
The advertising message is more believable for a smaller group of consumers.
Consumers with similar needs and values are more likely to respond to the offer.
Advertisers can't effectively market to different groups of consumers at the same time.
explanation: Consumers with similar needs and values are more likely to respond to the offer. Advertisers use research to group consumers with certain similarities and then speak to them in ways that are meaningful to them. Advertising believability does not relate to the size of audience to whom it is directed, and while some con-sumers may resist categorization for personal reasons, most are unaware of exactly how marketers and advertisers are grouping and describing them. Most advertisers do market their goods and services to differ-ent groups and use targeted approaches to do this effectively.

prompt: One of the main reasons for developing a marketing plan is to identify the strategies necessary to achieve the marketing
explanation: Objectives. Marketing objectives are the goals an advertising business seeks to reach with its marketing plan which is a set of strategies for attracting the target customer to the business. One of the main reasons for developing a marketing plan is to identify those strategies that are the plans of action for achieving mar-keting goals and objectives. Marketing functions are interrelated activities that must work together to get goods and services from producers to consumers. Marketing mix is the combination of the four elements of marketing—product, place, promotion, and price. Market share is an organization's portion of the total industry sales in a specific market.

prompt: The direct-mail company projected that its sales would increase significantly over the next few years, and it decided to
explanation: Hire more workers. One of the ways direct-mail businesses use sales forecasts is in determining whether or not to hire more workers. A projected sales increase would support the hiring of additional employees. A forecast for increased sales would tell a business not to raise its prices, lower inventory levels, or borrow operating funds.

prompt: All of the following are advantages of the Delphi technique of sales forecasting except that it can
choices: be repeated until the forecast is complete.
keep forceful individuals from dominating others.
gather opinions from those who won't speak out in groups.
explanation: Be repeated until the forecast is complete. In some cases, the group must be polled until it reaches agree-ment and the forecast can be completed. This is not an advantage because it can take a lot of time and cause the method to be an expensive one to use. The ability to gather opinions from those who might not speak up in a group, to prevent arguments and/or lengthy discussions by using questionnaires, and to keep forceful individuals from dominating others by using secret ballots are all advantages of the Delphi technique.

prompt: A client has telephoned the public relations agency with a question that the employee receiving the call cannot answer. Which of the following is the most appropriate response for the employee to make:
choices: "If you'll hold on, I'll see if anyone can answer that."
"That's a good question, and I'll get the answer for you."
"I don't know, but you can call back when my boss is here."
"There isn't anyone here now who can answer that question."
explanation: "That's a good question, and I'll get the answer for you." Clients often call public relations agencies with inquiries that the employee answering the telephone cannot answer. The employee should, however, not say "I don't know," as that may be the only part of the response that the client hears. Instead, a comment on the validity of the question and an offer to obtain the answer are better responses. Asking the client to hold while the employee tries to find the answer or to call later are unsatisfactory ways of handling client inquiries. Telling the client there is no one on hand who can answer the question is not a satisfactory way to handle a client inquiry because it does not help the client.

prompt: One reason why individuals might resist change is because they
choices: want to impress members of management.
have deep respect for the change agent.
are concerned over possible personal losses.
want to increase their chances of getting a promotion.
explanation: Are concerned over possible personal losses. Individuals might fear that they will personally experience a loss if organizational change occurs. This loss could come in the form of status, money, authority, friend-ships, or other benefits they value. Impressing management, respecting the change agent, and getting a promotion are reasons why individuals accept change.

prompt: The number of people who are supervised by an individual is called
explanation: Span of control. In most advertising companies, lower level management has a wider span of control, or more employees to supervise, than top management. Accountability is the employee's responsibility to carry out his/her assigned tasks. Unity of command means no employee reports to more than one supervisor. Line-and-staff organization is a method of business organization that includes specialists in each department.

prompt: One benefit of establishing a promotionfromwithin policy is that it
choices: reduces the need for ongoing training.
explanation: Increases employee loyalty. A commitment to the promotion of internal job candidates motivates employees to prepare for promotional opportunities and leads to more loyal employees. However, the most qualified people might be external candidates. Promoting from within often reduces salary expense because external recruits may expect higher incomes. Promoting from within does not reduce the need for ongoing training.

prompt: To verify information about applicants, employers can
explanation: Check references. The checking of references is a common method of gathering and of verifying information about applicants. Types of reference checks that are often used are previous employment, credit, education, and personal references. The information provided by applicants in résumés and in application blanks is verified through the use of reference checks. Physical examinations are used to identify applicants' pre existing health problems.

prompt: Media production companies that teach employees specific skills are providing the employees with
explanation: Training. Training is teaching or developing a specific skill. It helps workers to develop their own aptitudes, or abilities. Mentoring occurs when an experienced employee acts as a guide to a new employee. Providing employees with mentors gives them support, or backing.

prompt: One way for management to build high morale among employees is to
choices: use staff meetings to solve individual problems.
encourage employees' use of the company grapevine.
be sure all employees are treated in the same way.
keep the company's channels of communication open.
explanation: Keep the company's channels of communication open. One way to build and maintain a high level of morale among employees is to make sure that the channels of communication between supervisors and employees and between employees and supervisors are equally accessible. Management should also spot and correct rumors, rather than allowing false information to be passed through the company grapevine. Employees should be treated as individuals and recognized for their unique abilities. Staff meetings should address issues that apply to all employees. Individual problems should be solved in private.

prompt: A method that management can use to involve employees in decision making is to
explanation: Set up quality circles. Quality circles are problem-solving groups of coworkers who are given work situations or problems to study and discuss in order to recommend solutions to management. Participating in these groups gives employees the feeling that they are involved in the firm's decision making. Orientation acquaints new employees with their surroundings and their specific job responsibilities. Setting goals for employees to reach or offering them rewards for reaching those goals does not involve employees in decision making.

prompt: Photography studios that do not keep track of the quantity of supplies in stock may run out and be forced to
explanation: Place expensive rush orders. Photography studios should try to keep in stock the proper quantity of supplies. Running out of operating supplies may force studios to buy locally or place rush orders that often are expensive. Suppliers that handle rush orders usually charge a premium price for quick delivery. Therefore, not keeping track of the quantity of supplies in stock may be costly to studios. Photography studios that run out of supplies are not ordinarily forced to go out of business, to stop selling services, or to recruit additional personnel.

prompt: A specialty advertising business with monthly sales of $265,500 is offering a 1.5% discount for payment within 15 days to increase its cash flow. Calculate the amount the discount will reduce revenue.
explanation: $3,982.50. Specialty advertising businesses often analyze the accounts receivable component of cash flow in order to find ways to speed up the flow of cash into the business. One way to encourage customers to pay quickly is to offer discounts. The discounts reduce the amount of revenue the business receives, but this disadvantage may be offset by the increase in cash flow. If a business with monthly sales of $265,500 offers a 1.5% discount for payment within 15 days and all customers take advantage of the discount, the business will lose $3,982.50 in revenue. To calculate this amount, multiply the amount of sales by the discount ($265,500 x 1.5% or .015 = $3,982.50).

prompt: Kay has prepared a projected cash flow statement for a photography studio she plans to open. She has also prepared a second cash flow statement in which she projected lower revenues and higher expenses than she really expects. What is the purpose of this second statement?
choices: To show Kay she really should not open a business
To show the bankers that Kay has planned for every situation
To help Kay know how much cash she needs if business is worse than expected
To help Kay know how much cash she will have if business is better than expected
explanation: To help Kay know how much cash she needs if business is worse than expected. The "worst-case" scenario will help Kay determine how much cash would be needed if revenues were lower than expected or expenses were higher than expected. This allows Kay to determine how much cash will be generated in this situation. She would not prepare a second cash flow statement for the other reasons.

prompt: Individuals who work in advertising generally need to be articulate, energetic, and outgoing because
choices: intelligence is not as important as personality characteristics in advertising.
advertising is a fast-paced industry that requires a lot of communication and contact with all kinds of people.
studies have shown that advertising produced by outgoing individuals is more effective than that of more reserved people.
talkative, extroverted individuals are usually more successful and sought-after than their more introverted counterparts.
explanation: Advertising is a fast-paced industry that requires a lot of communication and contact with all kinds of people. Common wisdom says that energetic, outgoing individuals are more likely to thrive in an active, sometimes frenetic, environment with lots of stimulation (noise, people). Additionally, being articulate is a must for one to participate in the constant exchange of ideas and opinions. There is no evidence to suggest that talkative, extroverted individuals are more successful and sought-after than their quieter peers. Intelligence is equally important to personality factors in advertising. There are no studies demonstrating that outgoing individuals produce more effective advertising than people who are more reserved.

prompt: What do employees need to be successful in most business careers?
explanation: Basic academic skills. Basic academic skills involve the ability to read, write, perform simple math calcula-tions, and communicate verbally. Employees in most business careers, such as advertising, are expected to be able to read instructions or other business and promotional materials. They often need to write simple reports or record information and prepare sales checks or calculate prices. Business employees also need to be able to communicate verbally with coworkers and customers. These basic academic skills are needed to succeed in the business world. Physical strength is not usually a requirement for success in business. Apprenticeship training is necessary for many jobs in the trade industries. Technical backgrounds are helpful for jobs in specialized areas such as engineering.

prompt: Which of the following advertising careers involves working with radio and television stations to place commercials:
explanation: Media buyer. Media buyers are responsible for buying time on radio and television, and space in print pub-lications. Media buyers negotiate the best possible price for their clients' commercials or print advertise-ments. They also work to have the commercial aired at an effective time during the broadcast schedule and the print ad placed in a favorable location in the publication. A film editor is involved in the production of a commercial. Graphic designers and art directors are involved in creating the print advertisement.

prompt: Professional organizations and trade associations are groups formed by people who have similar needs and interests based on their common
explanation: Business interests or careers. Professional organizations and trade associations are formed specifically to unite people with similar business interests or careers. Members of individual organizations or associations may also have other factors in common such as training, education, or experience.

prompt: The determination of an exchange figure acceptable to both the buyer and the seller of an advertising good or service is called
explanation: Pricing. Pricing is the determination of an exchange price at which the buyer and seller perceive optimum value for a good or service. Promotion stimulates demand for products by informing customers of the prod-ucts' availability. Place decision is the marketing element focusing on considerations in getting a selected product in the right place at the right time. Product decision refers to what goods, services, or ideas a busi-ness will offer its customers.

prompt: Why is price such a critical factor in the relationship between an advertising agency and its clients?
choices: Clients think agencies charge too little for their services.
Clients believe that agencies are inefficient and unreliable.
Clients do not think that agencies charge fairly or honestly.
Clients often have trouble understanding the price of services.
explanation: Clients often have trouble understanding the price of services. Advertising agencies provide many services whose value and results are difficult to measure. The workings of an advertising agency are complex, with many different people, functions, and skill levels. Each type of service is priced differently. Agencies also purchase many different services from complementary providers and may charge for the management or oversight of these services, in addition to the service itself. These factors make it difficult at times for clients to reconcile their charges, along with the fact that the value and results of advertising services are frequently hard to measure. Some clients think agencies charge too much. Most clients believe agencies are efficient, reliable, and charge fairly and honestly even though they sometimes have trouble understanding the prices.

prompt: The point at which the promotional business's revenue from sales is equal to the total costs of generating that revenue is the
explanation: Breakeven point. After a promotional business reaches the break-even point, it begins to earn a profit because it has recovered its costs. If sales do not reach this point, the business will lose money and may fail. The point of no return is the time at which it is too late to go back, and the individual or business must go forward. Point-sales quota is a type of sales-volume quota in which salespeople receive a number of points for each dollar or product sold. Equilibrium point is reached when sellers offer the quantity and prices that are equal to those demanded by buyers.

prompt: Under which of the following circumstances might an outdoor advertising business decide to use a skimming price strategy to introduce a new product:
explanation: Limited competition. A skimming price strategy involves setting prices at very high levels for a short time. Outdoor advertising businesses often use a skimming price strategy to introduce a new product and quickly recover the costs of developing and producing the new product. A skimming price strategy is only effective in a few situations such as when a business has limited or no competition for the new product. Under those circumstances, customers must pay the high price if they want to buy the new product because it is not available elsewhere. Once competitors enter the market, a business that is using a skimming price strategy will need to lower its prices in order to remain competitive. Businesses usually set low prices if there is an excessive supply of an item or if there is insufficient demand for it. National distribution does not have an effect on whether a business would use a skimming price strategy.

prompt: One factor an agency manager considers when establishing the pricing for advertising services the agency offers is the
explanation: Agency's operating expenses. Many factors are considered when prices are established by ad agencies. Along with economic factors (e.g., demand) and competitor's rates, the manager must consider the operating costs, which include costs associated with running the facility, taxes, equipment and supplies, and salaries. In order to make money, the manager must know agency expenses incurred to produce the service. A client's line of credit, the agency's banking procedures, and a client's stock value are not considered when establishing pricing.

prompt: Why is obtaining, maintaining, or increasing market share important to a promotional business?
choices: A large market share ensures large profits.
Consumers are interested in a firm's market share.
Market share serves as a measure of the success of the business.
Market share must constantly increase in order for the business to succeed.
explanation: Market share serves as a measure of the success of the business. Many promotional businesses feel that the size of their share of the market is so important that they set specific goals for obtaining or increasing market share. Most consumers are unaware of or uninterested in a firm's share of the market. Having a large share of the market may lead to large profits, but there is no guarantee that this will happen. It is not necessary for market share to increase constantly in order for the business to be successful. Some busi-nesses simply try to maintain their share of the market by keeping their prices at a stable level.

prompt: Which of the following could be used to determine when price changes are necessary in order to meet competition:
explanation: Comparing prices. Businesses usually monitor competitors' prices and often adjust their own prices in order to gain or maintain market share. Obtaining information about the prices that others in the advertising indus-try charge is an effective way to adjust prices to remain competitive. Leader pricing is a pricing technique that sets prices near or below cost to attract customers. Price lining is a pricing technique that sets prices at predetermined price points.

prompt: During which of the following stages in a promotional product's life cycle can businesses expect to earn significant profits:
explanation: Growth. Growth is the product life-cycle stage in which sales rise rapidly. During that stage, businesses can expect an increase in sales which results in significant profits. The introduction stage is when the product first appears in the marketplace. Decline is the stage in which sales and profits fall rapidly. Maturity is the stage where the product reaches a plateau.

prompt: Which of the following is designed to protect consumers in any dealings they may have with collection agencies:
explanation: Fair Debt Collection Act. This law, passed in 1980, makes it a federal offense for a debt collector to harass or abuse consumers who owe them money. The Fair Credit Billing Act establishes procedures for consumers and creditors to follow when billing errors occur on statements. The TruthinLending Act provides specific disclosure requirements for the annual percentage rate and the finance charge as a dollar amount. The Fair Credit Reporting Act requires disclosure to consumers of the name and address of any agency that supplied reports used to deny credit, insurance, or employment.

prompt: Which of the following is a service that many advertising agencies offer their clients:
explanation: Traffic management. Many advertising agencies have a traffic department that is responsible for routing and scheduling work so that jobs are completed on time. Traffic management is an important service because if deadlines are missed, a client's advertisement might not run on time. The traffic department coordinates production and makes sure that media deadlines are met. Motor coordination is the harmonious use of muscles to accomplish a task. Needs assessment is a process of identifying and prioritizing training and development needs. Sales development involves identifying customers and building the business.

prompt: One reason why a creative boutique might concentrate its product-mix strategy on one type of product is to
explanation: Dominate the market. Many creative boutiques concentrate on one type of product, such as copywriting. In many cases, this product-mix strategy enables the boutique to dominate that particular market. The bou-tique's name becomes synonymous with the copywriting, and when clients think of the boutique, they think of the specific boutique. Boutiques that successfully use this type of strategy often obtain the majority of the market share. A boutique does not concentrate its product-mix strategy on one type of product to arrange for credit, provide a discount, or manage the demand.

prompt: A name, term, symbol, or design that identifies a product and distinguishes it from competitors' products is a
explanation: Brand. Brands help to sell products by creating images that are appealing and desirable to consumers. Generic products have no brand name and are usually priced lower than brand-name products. A patent is legal protection of an invention or a process granted by government to its owners for a certain number of years. A copyright is legal protection of books and other artistic works granted by government and giving their creators sole rights to them for 28 years.

prompt: An advertising agency is developing a survey to evaluate client satisfaction. What is true regarding the formation of the survey's questions?
choices: It is best to use true/false questions for surveys.
The survey should include no more than 15 questions.
Closed-end questions should be specific and performance oriented.
An equal number of open-ended and closed-end questions should be used.
explanation: Closed-end questions should be specific and performance oriented. Most people do not like to take the time to complete surveys. When using this evaluation method, closed-end questions can be formatted to obtain specific information in regards to service and performance levels. A good example is, "Did the representative answer the telephone in three rings and in a courteous manner?" An example of a less desirable question is, "How did the representative answer the telephone?" There are no data to indicate that it is better to use an equal number of open-ended and closed-end questions, that true/false questions are best, and that 15 or fewer questions should be included.

prompt: Why is it important for advertisers to carefully research foreign languages and customs before promoting their products in other countries?
choices: Adapting promotions to foreign use will eliminate the possibility of damaging company sales and reputation.
Promotion in foreign countries will usually require developing entirely new ideas, as opposed to adapting ones used here.
Foreign consumers are usually amused by promotions that make mistakes with their language or culture.
Ideas and concepts often do not translate exactly and may communicate something incorrect or offensive when translated into another language.
explanation: Ideas and concepts often do not translate exactly and may communicate something incorrect or offensive when translated into another language. Advertisers can cite countless instances of failed promotions due to incomplete knowledge or poor understanding of foreign languages and cultures. Promotion in foreign coun-tries may require developing entirely new ideas, but in many cases, promotional concepts used here can be successfully adapted to foreign use. Even when promotions are adapted, however, problems can still occur if all the cultural nuances are not taken into account. Most of the time, foreign consumers are not amused by promotions that make errors having to do with their language or culture. Not only does this directly impact product image and sales, it is also perceived by many in other countries to be cultural arrogance on the part of companies or a sign of disrespect for their cultures.

prompt: In order to communicate with the consumers who are most likely to buy their products, marketers first need to
explanation: Identify their target audience. Communication must be appropriate to the receiver in order for it to be effective. This means that marketers must identify their target audience, or target market, and plan their communications for that audience. Studying their own industry might be part of identifying the target audience. Evaluating past ads and choosing media are other steps in the promotional communication process.

prompt: Which of the following government agencies monitors deceptive and unfair advertising in order to protect consumers and promote competition:
explanation: Federal Trade Commission. The Federal Trade Commission (FTC) administers and enforces antitrust laws and consumer-protection laws. It is the agency with the most influence on marketing activities such as pro-motion and advertising. The FTC prohibits businesses from misrepresenting their products in advertisements, making unsubstantiated claims, and otherwise misleading consumers. The FTC may require businesses to place corrective ads to explain deceptive information. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) grants licenses to radio and television stations and regulates interstate telephone and telegraph rates and service. The Better Business Bureau and the National Advertising Review Council are nongovernmental agencies.

prompt: A warm color that can be used in advertising to catch customers' attention is
explanation: Yellow. Yellow is an eye-catching color that is considered a warm color, in part because of its association with sunlight. Blue and green are cool colors. White is not a warm color and is only attention-getting when used in contrast with a dark color such as black.

prompt: Repeated exposure to the largest, most diverse population of people is a benefit of ___________ advertising.
explanation: Out-of-home. Certain spots (e.g., bus stations) outside of the home attract a large percentage of people from different backgrounds, thereby providing the perfect opportunity to expose them to a message over and over again. Radio advertisements last for only as long as they are on the air, and they are targeted at a very specific group of listeners. Once people are finished reading newspapers, they typically throw them away. In addition, not as many people read newspapers as drive by public places over and over again. Directory advertising is a great opportunity to appeal to people who are looking for the business's contact information, but rarely is there repeated exposure to an ad.

prompt: The advertising headline "Wendy's Restaurant Opening Today" would be classified as a __________ headline.
explanation: News. A news headline focuses on whatever is new or newsworthy about a product or a company. This head-line gives readers the news that Wendy's will be open. A curiosity headline hints at the content of the ad so that the reader will want to read further. A benefit headline promises the reader a benefit or the solution to a problem. A testimonial headline is a statement made by an expert or a celebrity about a product or company.

prompt: A guideline to follow in preparing the copy for a newspaper ad is to
choices: use the advertising copy provided by suppliers.
write the ad from the viewpoint of the customer.
provide detailed explanations of the product(s).
explanation: Write the ad from the viewpoint of the customer. An advertiser must consider not only what products to advertise but also the reactions of consumers being reached by the ad. Writing from the customer's view-point helps to draw the customer into the ad and makes it more personal. Advertising copy and illustrations should reflect the image of your business and not just that of a supplying firm. Avoid lengthy and detailed product explanations in your copy. Testimonials are not always available to use.

prompt: One of the reasons that some businesses select a photograph of the product in use to include in an advertisement is to communicate the product's
explanation: Features and benefits. Photographs of a product being used communicate the product's features and bene-fits to consumers. The visual representation of a product in action graphically shows customers how they might benefit from a product's features. For example, a photograph might show a person emerging unhurt from an accident because of an automobile air bag. Research and development activities are communicated with words and figures. Slogans and trademarks are communicated by words and/or drawings. Design is presented through sketches, and production is expressed in statistics.

prompt: In preparing an advertisement, which of the following layouts should be completed first:
explanation: Thumbnail sketch. The thumbnail sketch is the first stage in the development of an ad layout. This is little more than a line drawing to show how the elements of the ad will be arranged. Next comes the rough draft, which is drawn to the size scale of the actual ad and is much more detailed. The comprehensive layout is a refined version of the rough draft that is approved by the client before the final layout is prepared. The final layout may be called a mechanical, paste-up, keyline, or working layout.

prompt: What is the frequency if 24,000 people are exposed to five magazine ads, and 76,000 people are exposed to five television commercials?
explanation: 5. Frequency is defined as the average number of times a person in the target audience is exposed to an advertising message. Average frequency is determined by dividing the total number of exposures by the total number of people reached. In this example, 24,000 people were exposed to five magazine ads for a total of 120,000 exposures (24,000 x 5 = 120,000), and 76,000 people were exposed to five television commercials for a total of 380,000 exposures (76,000 x 5 = 380,000). Total the number of people reached (24,000 + 76,000 = 100,000), and the exposures (120,000 + 380,000 = 500,000). Divide the total number of exposures by the total number of people reached to determine frequency (500,000 ÷ 100,000 = 5).

prompt: A local business buys the following radio time: five 10-second spots during daytime, six 15-second spots during morning drive, and three 10-second spots during evening drive. Based on the following information, determine the cost of the radio time: 10-second spots 15-second spots Morning drive $55.00 $72.50 Daytime $30.50 $45.25 Evening drive $58.25 $75.00 Nighttime $27.50 $31.25 All night $22.00 $28.50
explanation: $762.25. Most radio stations divide radio time into specific dayparts and charge businesses different prices for advertising during various times. Certain dayparts are more expensive than others because they usually attract larger audiences. The stations also charge different prices depending on the length of the spots. To calculate the cost of the radio time in this example, first determine the total cost of the various spots. The cost of one 10-second spot during daytime is $30.50; therefore, the cost of five spots is $152.50 ($30.50 x 5 = $152.50). The cost of one 15-second spots during morning drive is $72.50; therefore, six spots cost $435.00 ($72.50 x 6 = $435.00). The cost of one 10-second spot during evening drive is $58.25; therefore, three spots cost $174.75 ($58.25 x 3 = $174.75). Add the totals to determine the cost of the radio time ($152.50 + $435.00 + $174.75 = $762.25).

prompt: The business owner checked proofs for the business's new magazine advertisement in order to
explanation: Correct any errors. Businesses check advertising proofs in order to make sure that the ad looks and reads as it was intended, and to correct any errors. Checking proofs is the last chance a business has to make any changes before the ad appears in print. The purpose of proofing ads is to look for final errors and not to change the visuals, rewrite the copy, or alter the typestyle. Decisions about these elements should have been made long before the proof stage.

prompt: The travel section of Sunday newspapers is an effective place for airlines, bus companies, and cruise lines to advertise their services because it
explanation: Is read by potential customers. The travel section of Sunday newspapers is an effective place for travel com-panies to advertise because people thinking about traveling often read that section in order to get ideas, compare prices, and find out what is currently available. People frequently book trips or make travel reserva-tions by contacting the transportation companies that advertise in the travel section, which is designed specif-ically to appeal to people interested in travel. Transportation companies do not advertise in the travel section because it contains colorful photographs or promotes competitive pricing. The travel section is intended for travelers, which might include businesspeople, although businesspeople are not the main audience.

prompt: Why do we say that publicity has no sponsor?
choices: Because brand names are not used in publicity
Because businesses are not mentioned in publicity
Because no one pays the media to present publicity
Because no one pays the business for publicity items
explanation: Because no one pays the media to present publicity. A sponsor is a business, individual, or organization that pays the costs of promotion. Publicity has no sponsor because no one pays the media to present the pub-licity. The media do not pay the businesses for their items because the media are doing the businesses a favor. Brand names and the names of businesses are often used in publicity items.

prompt: The most effective brochure for a local AA baseball team will contain which of the following elements:
explanation: Table of discounts. The most effective brochures contain elements that link price with value. The table of discounts will emphasize special promotions for groups, children, and seniors. Information about discounts is more important than the name of the stadium. Statistics of players change and would be unnecessary to include in the brochure. Sponsors of the team would be included because they provide financial backing; however, this information does not add to the effectiveness of the brochure.

prompt: Ford Motor Company's "Quality is Job 1!" is an example of a promotional
explanation: Slogan. A slogan is a short, memorable phrase that promotes a company's philosophy and/or its products. In this instance, Ford is emphasizing the importance of quality in its vehicles. A logotype, or trademark, is a symbol, design, or word used by a business to identify a good or service. A brand name is the part of a brand that can be spoken, such as a word, a phrase, a letter, a number, or any combination of these.

prompt: Part of coordinating a business's promotional activities so that they will achieve the business's promotional goals is informing salespeople about
choices: who selected the products being promoted.
how much is being spent on all activities.
how many customers are expected to respond.
what promotional activities will take place.
explanation: What promotional activities will take place. Coordinating promotional activities so that they work together to sell products is important to achieving promotional goals. Part of this effort should include providing sales-people with complete information about what promotional activities will take place, when they will occur, and how long they will last. This information will help salespeople to prepare to sell the products that are being promoted. Salespeople do not need to know who selected the products for promotion or how much is being spent on the promotional activities. Customer response can only be estimated, at best, and is not essential information.

prompt: What might be the result if a business allocates most of its advertising budget to promoting a few major sales events?
choices: Most sales will occur during that time
Not enough funds for weekly advertising
Not likely to qualify for cooperative funds
explanation: Not enough funds for weekly advertising. When a business chooses to spend most of its advertising funds for certain events, the business may not have enough funds to support a program of regular weekly ads throughout the year. It is generally considered to be a more effective use of advertising funds when a busi-ness spreads its advertising throughout the year. Promoting only a few major events does not mean that most sales will occur during that time or that competitors will increase their advertising. A business focusing on special sales could qualify for cooperative advertising funds if they were available for the products to be sold at those times.

prompt: Why is a situation analysis such a critical part of an advertising campaign plan?
choices: The situation analysis includes geographic strategies, timing, and a budget.
The situation analysis combines select information from the other sections.
The situation analysis identifies key problems to be solved and objectives that will accomplish those tasks.
The situation analysis includes all the foundation information for the campaign plan upon which the other elements are built.
explanation: The situation analysis includes all the foundation information for the campaign plan upon which the other elements are built. The situation analysis looks at research findings, competition, consumers, and the market-place in order to "set the stage" for the solutions that will follow in the rest of the plan for the campaign. The situation analysis does not pull information from other sections into it, but instead is focused on building the platform from which the other sections spring. The strategy section of a campaign plan identifies key problems and objectives, not the situational analysis; and it is the media section of the plan, not the situation analysis, that includes geographic strategies, timing, and budget considerations.

prompt: The advantage of providing news releases to appropriate media outlets prior to the kickoff of a major advertising campaign is that it can
choices: eliminate the need to write feature stories and corporate newsletters.
control the way the media presents product information to the audience.
provide additional challenges and opportunities for the campaign copywriter.
disburse potentially free press coverage, which may generate product awareness.
explanation: Disburse potentially free press coverage, which may generate product awareness. Because advertising efforts are so expensive, it is in the best interest of the sponsor to take advantage of venues that provide free media coverage. Print publications often need space fillers for pieces, and broadcast media such as television and radio make public-service announcements. By letting media outlets know of new products, advancements, and community service activities, there is potential for reinforcement of the sponsor's brand image. Media outlets incorporate press releases to build positive relationships with sponsors, hoping for the sponsor to purchase additional advertising space. Most press releases are prepared by the public-relations staff and are not generally prepared to give the campaign copywriter additional challenges and opportunities. Press releases do not eliminate the need for feature stories or corporate newsletters. Feature stories are usually generated by the media outlet, not the sponsor or advertising agency. Ideally, sponsors should use every appropriate method of promotion, including newsletters. Media outlets can edit a news release once it is received. Therefore, the sponsor does not have control over the way product information is presented to an audience.

prompt: What effect does building a clientele have on a specialty advertising business's selling costs?
choices: Reduces them because salespeople earn more in bonuses and commissions
Increases them because salespeople earn less in bonuses and commissions
Reduces them because making a repeat sale costs less than making an initial sale
Increases them because making an initial sale costs more than making a repeat sale
explanation: Reduces them because making a repeat sale costs less than making an initial sale. Because of reduced selling costs, it is to the specialty advertising business's advantage to develop a loyal clientele. Repeat sales to a client are more profitable for the business. With repeat sales, salespeople are usually able to increase their commissions and bonuses.

prompt: One way that governments often control selling practices in a private enterprise system is by
choices: mandating that all businesses structure ownership as corporations.
establishing regulations that make it difficult to enter a specific market.
reviewing each sales transaction that exceeds a set amount in dollars and volume.
requiring that all businesses provide government access to their computer databases.
explanation: Establishing regulations that make it difficult to enter a specific market. A private enterprise system is an economic system in which individuals and groups, rather than government, own or control the means of production—the human and natural resources and capital goods used to produce goods and services. Many governments develop regulations and act as referee between producers, intermediaries, and consumers. Establishing regulations can make it difficult to enter a given market, but not impossible. For example, there are regulations that restrict who is able to own and operate radio and television stations. Mandating owner-ship structure and requiring government access to business information are not characteristics of a private or semiprivate enterprise system. It is unrealistic to expect a government in a large private enterprise system to review each sales transaction that occurs.

prompt: Why is having a great deal of information about specialty advertising products advantageous to making sales?
choices: So that salespeople can use jargon to impress customers
Because product information is not readily available to final consumers
Because salespeople will be able to send the information to consumers rather than meet with them
So that the salesperson will have the ability to tailor sales presentations to individual customers
explanation: So that the salesperson will have the ability to tailor sales presentations to individual customers. In order for specialty advertising salespeople to be effective, they must be able to determine the needs and wants of their customers and match the features and benefits of the product to those needs and wants. Salespeople would be unable to do this if they were uninformed about the product. Although product information is avail-able to consumers, they often count on salespeople to act as their experts. Jargon usually should not be used in sales presentations, especially if the customer is not very familiar with the product. Product informa-tion is not used in place of a sales presentation, but rather as an aid to make the presentation better.

prompt: What do many media salespeople develop to prepare an effective and persuasive sales presentation?
explanation: Visual aids. Visual aids are often an important part of an effective sales presentation. Some information is better explained with the help of visuals such as charts, graphs, photographs, videos, etc. Many media salespeople spend a great deal of time developing visual aids that help them to attract and hold the attention of their customers. Other types of visuals include promotional brochures and pamphlets that a salesperson can leave with customers. Visual aids can be important selling aids if they are well developed and properly used. Account quotas are established by management. Bonus plans are a form of compensation. Sales-people often prepare reports after calling on customers.

prompt: While listening to clients, advertising account representatives should be
choices: ready to interrupt at any time.
explanation: Trying to maintain eye contact. Maintaining eye contact does not mean staring fixedly at clients, but it does mean looking them in the eye and meeting their gaze when they look at you. You should listen without interrupting in order to understand what clients are saying, rather than planning your response. Clients are concerned with their own views—not with yours.

prompt: During which phase of the selling process do specialty advertising salespeople try to prove to customers that their goods or services will satisfy the customers' wants and needs?
explanation: Feature-benefit selling. An important part of specialty advertising salespeople's jobs is to determine what each customer is looking for in a good or service. Then, salespeople must prove to customers that their goods or services have the features that will benefit the customers. This phase of the selling process is referred to as feature-benefit selling. This phase can occur at any time during the selling process. Salespeople usually try to address customers' individual needs before explaining the features and benefits of goods or services. Trading-up selling involves selling a higher price line than the original request because it would meet the customer's real needs. Suggesting substitute items involves suggesting a product other than the original request when the business does not have the item requested or when the salesperson recognizes the cus-tomer's true needs.

prompt: Outdoor advertising salespeople should avoid overselling because it tends to
explanation: Interfere with buying decisions. Overselling often leaves customers in a state of indecision because too many features or benefits are presented. This causes sales to be lost. Overselling creates a negative atmosphere. When salespeople oversell, they appear more interested in making sales than in satisfying customer needs.

prompt: What type of advertising service might an agency account representative recommend to a client who wants help developing and organizing information for an annual report?
explanation: Copywriting. Advertising agencies offer a variety of services, all of which are not needed by every client. Copywriting is one of those services and involves researching, writing, and editing written materials for docu-ments such as annual reports, promotional brochures, and news releases. If a client needs help developing information for an annual report, an account representative should recommend the agency’s copywriting services. Once the annual report is written, the agency might arrange to have it printed. The agency would not market or schedule the report.

prompt: Often, printing salespeople who are prospecting can obtain lists of current and past customers, credit records, and inquiries from
explanation: Their own companies. Printing salespeople should make use of information available from within their own companies before looking outside. Noncompeting salespeople and trade associations usually do not have access to information about your current or past customers, their credit records, or their product inquiries. The Wall Street Journal is a business trade paper that contains such information as stock prices, advertising, science, money matters, and national and international business news.

prompt: A salesperson for a television station submits a sales report containing the following information that the station uses to determine compensation: $65,000 monthly sales, 15 total sales, and 90 appointments. If the station uses this information to determine compensation and the salesperson is paid 5% commission, what is the monthly compensation?
explanation: $3,250. Television stations often use sales-report information as a basis for compensating salespeople. Depending on company requirements, sales reports may contain a variety of information such as actual appointments, leads generated, follow-up calls, number of sales, and total dollar value of the sales. The revenue that salespeople generate is usually the figure that stations use to determine compensation. In this situation, the salesperson was paid a 5% commission on total monthly sales of $65,000. To determine actual compensation, multiply the sales figure by 5% ($65,000 x 5% or .05 = $3,250).

prompt: Which of the following do public relations agencies often call upon to assist with sales training:
explanation: Consultants. Public relations agencies often call upon consultants, or outside specialists, to assist with sales training. Consultants may establish and administer a customized program or design sales training to be implemented by others in the organization. This can minimize training costs since it is purchased on an asneeded basis. Agencies do not obtain assistance with sales training from stockholders or competitors. A subsidiary is a company that is wholly owned and controlled by another company.
